title.purpose: The page title only, one per view.

body.purpose: Form controls, tabs, descriptions, runtime status.

label.purpose: Field labels, help text, contact state words, proof lines, totals (400 to 600).

designator.purpose: REV, K1–K6, RB, settings keys, server error codes, version numbers.

shadows.name: raised-light
shadows.purpose: The one elevation (corporateLight, --ds-shadow-raised): panels and cards.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus: sheet-coloured halo plus a conductor-blue ring.

shadows.name: input-focus-glow
shadows.purpose: Soft tint around a focused field.

shadows.name: input-error-glow
shadows.purpose: Soft tint around a field in error.

motion.name: contact-blade
motion.purpose: A change-circuit contact closing or opening; the one authored motion on the configuration surface.

motion.name: contact-stagger
motion.purpose: Per-contact delay (index × 60ms) so contacts close in sequence.

motion.name: state-color
motion.purpose: Colour and background transitions on buttons, rows and tabs.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global rule: every transition and animation collapses; state still shows.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Change circuit becomes a sticky 20rem right column; below it is a horizontal strip.

knownLimits: No backup designator: the apply API returns no backup id, so the Backup contact shows "Taken before write" without a BK- number.
No live per-step progress: POST /api/config answers once, so Validate, Backup, Apply and Ready are Pending together while it runs.

narrative.overview:
NRCC is drawn the way a panel builder draws a control cabinet: IEC schematic language on a drawing-white sheet (the dark theme is the drawing negative), hairline ink conductors, and conductor colours that each do one job. The stylesheet names the world "Esquema eléctrico". The operator configures one Node-RED instance and must see what will happen before it happens, so the interface reads as a technical drawing they can trust, not as a dashboard of cards.

The signature is the change circuit: the gated sequence Edit → Diff → Validate → Backup → Apply → Ready drawn as six normally-open contacts on one conductor. A contact closes when its gate passes; a failure leaves it open and, when the server rolled back, draws the rollback branch. Every state is said in words and shape, never by colour alone. Density is a feature: three type sizes, ranked by weight, case and rule rather than by size.

Identity lives in designators, not decoration. The settings revision is `REV a1b2c3d4`, contacts are `K1`–`K6`, the rollback branch is `RB`, and every settings field carries its `settings.js` key as a terminal label. Light and dark are equal citizens; WCAG 2.2 AA holds in both.
keyCharacteristics: Flat drawing sheet, 1px hairlines, at most a 1px-offset shadow.
Conductor colours with fixed jobs: blue acts and selects, brown is pending, green-yellow fills a verified contact, red is critical and rollback only.
Three type sizes (20, 14, 12px) in Overpass; designators in Overpass Mono.
Stable mono designators (REV, K1–K6, RB, settings keys) instead of icons and badges.
Self-hosted fonts and assets; nothing loads from the network.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: A conductor colour means one thing everywhere: blue acts or selects, brown is pending, green and green-yellow are verified, red is critical or rollback, amber is a held gate. Never use a conductor colour as decoration.

rules.name: The Red Is Rare Rule
rules.body: Red appears only for a failure, a rollback, a destructive action or an error. A screen with no fault shows no red.

rules.name: The Tint Text Rule
rules.body: Text on a semantic tint or a plain surface uses the `*-text` value (`--ds-on-tint-*`), never the solid fill colour; the solid colour is for borders, fills and button grounds.

rules.name: The Three Sizes Rule
rules.body: Use only 20, 14 and 12px. Rank by weight, case and a rule line, never by adding a fourth size.

rules.name: The Tabular Data Rule
rules.body: Tables, code, counts and totals use tabular numerals so columns and digits never shift.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Elevation is a 1px border plus at most `--ds-shadow-raised`. If a surface needs more separation, use a ground change or a rule line, not a bigger shadow.

dos: **Do** give every colour one job from the One Job Rule, and say every state in text as well as colour and shape.

**Do** report the outcome of a gated configuration change on the change circuit and its polite live region. **No toasts on the gated flow**: applying, holding, failing and rolling back a change never raise a toast.
**Do** label settings with their `settings.js` key in mono, and identify things with stable designators (`REV`, `K1`–`K6`, `RB`).
**Do** use the control-border colour (`--ds-border-strong`) for every control edge and conductor, and the hairline only for decorative dividers.
**Do** keep to the three sizes (20, 14, 12px) and rank with weight, case and rule lines.

**Do** derive every circuit state from a signal the product really observes. The transaction is one request: while it runs, Validate, Backup, Apply and Ready are all Pending together, and an answer without a known error code leaves them Not confirmed.
**Do** keep fonts and assets self-hosted, and both themes at WCAG 2.2 AA.
donts: **Don't** invent a backup designator. The apply API returns no backup id, so the Backup contact's proof is "Taken before write" with no `BK-` number until the API exposes one.
**Don't** animate per-step progress inside the server transaction. The frontend sees only its start and its end, so no live per-step progress exists to draw.
**Don't** use red for anything but failure, rollback, destructive actions and errors.
**Don't** add gradients, glows, glass blur or shadows deeper than `--ds-shadow-raised`.
**Don't** wrap a settings key mid-word; break only after a dot.
